title: Unknown linear nonstochastic control: known stabilizer and strong controllability.
summary: The controller observes the full state and chooses an input for an unknown linear system driven by bounded disturbances. A stabilizing feedback matrix is known, and strong controllability is assumed. Performance is compared with the counterfactual trajectory of the best fixed stabilizing linear controller under the same disturbances. Interactions used for system identification are charged to the budget.

model.instance: $$x_{t+1}=Ax_t+Bu_t+w_t,\qquad x_t\in\mathbb R^{d_x},\quad u_t\in\mathbb R^{d_u},\quad x_0=0.$$ The matrices $A,B$ are fixed and unknown. The disturbance sequence is fixed before interaction and satisfies $\|w_t\|_2\le W$; independent random noise is not assumed. The cost functions $c_t(x,u)$ are fixed in advance, differentiable, and convex. For every radius $D\ge1$, $\|x\|_2,\|u\|_2\le D$ implies $\|\nabla c_t(x,u)\|_2\le GD$. A stabilizer $K_0$ is known, and the closed-loop system admits the decomposition $$A-BK_0=QLQ^{-1},\qquad \|L\|_2\le1-\gamma,\qquad 0<\gamma\le1,$$ $$\max\{\|A\|_2,\|B\|_2,\|K_0\|_2,\|Q\|_2,\|Q^{-1}\|_2\}\le C_{\mathrm{stab}}.$$ Strong controllability additionally requires the following matrix to have full row rank and satisfy $$C_k=[B,(A-BK_0)B,\ldots,(A-BK_0)^{k_{\mathrm{ctrl}}-1}B],\qquad \|(C_kC_k^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\|_2\le C_{\mathrm{ctrl}}.$$

description_paragraphs:
$$
x_{t+1}=Ax_t+Bu_t+w_t,\qquad x_t\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x},\quad u_t\in\mathbb{R}^{d_u},\quad x_0=0.
$$
The quantity $A,B$ is fixed and unknown. The disturbance sequence is fixed before interaction and satisfies $\|w_t\|_2\le W$; disturbances need not be independent random noise.

Cost functions $c_t(x,u)$ are fixed in advance, differentiable, and convex. For every radius $D\ge1$, $\|x\|_2,\|u\|_2\le D$ implies $\|\nabla c_t(x,u)\|_2\le GD$. The known stabilizer $K_0$ admits the following closed-loop decomposition:

$$
A-BK_0=QLQ^{-1},\qquad \|L\|_2\le1-\gamma,\qquad 0<\gamma\le1,
$$
Closed-loop strong controllability additionally requires the following matrix to have full row rank and satisfy:

$$
C_k=[B,(A-BK_0)B,\ldots,(A-BK_0)^{k_{\mathrm{ctrl}}-1}B],\qquad \|(C_kC_k^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\|_2\le C_{\mathrm{ctrl}}.
$$
Control times are consistently indexed by $t=0,\ldots,T-1$, giving T control actions and matching the initial state $x_0=0$.
model.parameter_domain_description: G: $G>0$ (public); T: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public); \delta_{\mathrm{conf}}: $0<\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}<1$ (public); d_x: $d_x\in\mathbb N,\ d_x\ge1$ (public); d_u: $d_u\in\mathbb N,\ d_u\ge1$ (public); W: $W\ge0$ (public); K_0: $K_0\in\mathbb R^{d_u\times d_x}$ (public); \gamma: $0<\gamma\le1$ (public); C_{\mathrm{stab}}: $C_{\mathrm{stab}}>0$ (public); k_{\mathrm{ctrl}}: $k_{\mathrm{ctrl}}\in\mathbb N,\ k_{\mathrm{ctrl}}\ge1$ (public); C_{\mathrm{ctrl}}: $C_{\mathrm{ctrl}}>0$ (public)

operations.query_signature: Observe the full state $x_t$, choose $u_t$, incur $c_t(x_t,u_t)$, and then receive the complete current cost function and next state. Neither $A,B$ nor the disturbance is directly revealed. Arbitrary causal controllers are allowed; the algorithm is not restricted to a particular linear feedback form. Inputs $d_x,d_u,T,G,W,K_0,\gamma,C_{\mathrm{stab}},C_{\mathrm{ctrl}},k_{\mathrm{ctrl}},\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$ are public. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

metric.base_expression: $$\begin{gathered}K\in\mathcal K\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \exists Q_K,L_K:\ A-BK=Q_KL_KQ_K^{-1},\\ \|L_K\|_2\le1-\gamma,\qquad \max\{\|A\|_2,\|B\|_2,\|K\|_2,\|Q_K\|_2,\|Q_K^{-1}\|_2\}\le C_{\mathrm{stab}}.\end{gathered}$$ $$R_T=\sum_t c_t(x_t,u_t)-\min_{K\in\mathcal K}\sum_t c_t(x_t^K,-Kx_t^K).$$
metric.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
metric.finiteness_conditions: Bounded disturbances and strongly stable comparators control the counterfactual benchmark. The source controller and its feasible system-identification phase provide the stated high-probability cost guarantee.
description_paragraphs:

R_T=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}c_t(x_t,u_t)-\min_{K\in\mathcal K}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}c_t(x_t^K,-Kx_t^K),\qquad x_{t+1}^K=(A-BK)x_t^K+w_t,\ x_0^K=0.
$$
